question: In relation to congenital hypothyroidism, indicate the statement FALSE:

options.opa: Neonatal screening programs detect most cases.
options.opb: A non-majority percentage of cases (around 10%) are transitory.
options.opc: Thyroid dyshormonogenesis are the most frequent causes.
options.opd: Thyroid dysgenesis are alterations in the embryonic development of the thyroid gland.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Neonatal screening programs detect most cases -> Early detection allows for prompt treatment -> Improves neurodevelopmental outcomes -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: A non-majority percentage of cases (around 10%) are transitory -> Transitory cases may resolve spontaneously -> Long-term treatment may not be necessary -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Thyroid dyshormonogenesis are the most frequent causes -> Genetic mutations in thyroid hormone synthesis enzymes -> Disrupts hormone production -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Thyroid dysgenesis are alterations in the embryonic development of the thyroid gland -> Results in structural abnormalities of the thyroid gland -> Impairs hormone production -> 95%
enhanced_information: In relation to congenital hypothyroidism, the FALSE statement is opc. Thyroid dyshormonogenesis are the most frequent causes. Contrary to the chain, thyroid dysgenesis, which are alterations in the embryonic development of the thyroid gland, are actually more common causes of congenital hypothyroidism. Evidence paths confirm the link between thyroid dysgenesis and structural abnormalities in the thyroid gland, leading to impaired hormone production.
analysis: Congenital hypothyroidism is a condition present at birth due to underactive thyroid function. The most common causes are related to thyroid dysgenesis, which involves structural abnormalities in the thyroid gland. Thyroid dyshormonogenesis, although a significant cause, is not the most frequent. Therefore, the statement opc is FALSE.
